title: Max Consecutive Ones III
statement: You may flip at most `k` zeros in the binary array `nums`. Return the maximum number of consecutive 1s you can produce.
hints: A window is valid when it contains at most k zeros.
Expand the right edge. When zeros exceed k, advance the left edge.
The longest valid window length is the answer.
editorial: This is the at-most-k variant of the sliding window. Count zeros inside the window. While the count exceeds k, move left and decrement when a zero leaves. Every valid window length is a candidate. Because both edges only move forward, the scan is linear.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def longest_ones(nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
    left = zeros = best = 0
    for right, value in enumerate(nums):
        zeros += value == 0
        while zeros > k:
            zeros -= nums[left] == 0
            left += 1
        best = max(best, right - left + 1)
    return best
